thingsToDo.title: Sand Hollow State Park
thingsToDo.description: Sand Hollow State Park is a Utah state park centered on Sand Hollow Reservoir with red sandstone terrain and open desert riding areas. it anchors Hurricane's outdoor economy by combining boating water access with nearby OHV terrain in one managed recreation zone. Common activities include paddling and boating on the reservoir, beach access along the shoreline, and guided or self-guided off-road routes in surrounding dunes. For Hurricane itineraries, this stop gives concrete context for how natural systems and public infrastructure shape the region's travel patterns, seasonal timing, and visitor access. thingsToDo.title: Quail Creek State Park
thingsToDo.description: Quail Creek State Park is a reservoir park west of Hurricane set below volcanic hills and managed for warm-water recreation and fishing. the lake is a stable, accessible water site in a desert region and plays a practical role in regional recreation planning. Visitors typically swim or paddle near boat ramps, fish for stocked species, and use day-use facilities for short stops between Zion-area and St. George routes. thingsToDo.title: Toquerville Falls
thingsToDo.description: Toquerville Falls is a waterfall feature in the Hurricane area reached by backcountry roads in a desert drainage landscape. it is a well-known local contrast point where perennial flow and rock shelves create a rare water-focused stop in otherwise arid terrain. Travelers usually arrive by high-clearance vehicle, view the falls from the natural rock basin, and combine the stop with other nearby off-pavement routes. thingsToDo.title: Gooseberry Mesa
thingsToDo.description: Gooseberry Mesa is a mesa south of Zion known for technical slickrock mountain-bike routes and broad desert-and-canyon viewpoints. it is a nationally recognized riding destination that shaped Hurricane's reputation in the Southwest bike-trail network. Riders use signed loops and connectors across slickrock shelves, while non-riders use trailheads and overlooks for short hikes and landscape photography. thingsToDo.title: Virgin River
thingsToDo.description: Virgin River is a tributary of the Colorado River that flows through southwest Utah and the Hurricane basin before entering Arizona and Nevada. the river system is fundamental to local settlement, irrigation history, and the canyon geomorphology that defines this part of the state. Visitors encounter it at parks, trail crossings, and scenic corridors, where it provides habitat context and links Hurricane to Zion and downstream desert communities. faq.q: How many days should I plan for Hurricane?
faq.a: Two to three days is enough for core Hurricane highlights plus one or two local experiences.

faq.q: Should I book tours ahead in Hurricane?
faq.a: Yes—advance booking is recommended for weekends, holidays, and top-rated operators.
